correctness.rationale: The final claim has one exact domain: ten-word binary (2,1)-separating systems of length eight. The prior maximum 10 was reconstructed from the inspected normalized closest-pair proof. For the new refinement, the package verifier exhaustively counts all distance-at-least-four ten-word systems containing zero (46,200), converts this by translation incidence to 1,182,720 labeled systems, directly validates three representatives, computes their exact stabilizers 48, 32, and 16 in the full Hamming-isometry group, and obtains disjoint orbit sizes summing to the full census. The coordinate pair-distance bound proves no ten-word binary code can have minimum distance at least five. The computation is finite and exhaustive; no timeout or partial enumeration is used.

value.rationale: This is a natural equality refinement of a standard exact coding-theory parameter: among all cardinality-optimal separating systems it determines the greatest simultaneous Hamming separation and completely classifies every system attaining that secondary optimum. The invariant is motivated by error separation inside an extremal fingerprinting/separating code, and the result supplies a full census and symmetry taxonomy rather than an arbitrary slice or a recomputation of the known maximum size.
